name: Gliomatosis cerebri

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: No formal consensus criteria; diagnosis based on clinical, radiological, and histopathological findings

criteria.description: Diffuse infiltration of at least three cerebral lobes by neoplastic glial cells
MRI showing diffuse T2/FLAIR hyperintensity involving multiple lobes without a discrete mass
Biopsy demonstrating glial tumor cells with low to high grade features diffusely infiltrating brain parenchyma
Progressive neurological deficits consistent with diffuse cerebral involvement

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of diffuse infiltration involving at least three cerebral lobes confirmed by MRI and histopathology
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is challenging due to diffuse nature; multiple biopsies may be required

pathognomonic.symptomName: Diffuse cerebral dysfunction with multifocal neurological deficits
searchTerms: widespread brain dysfunction with multiple nerve problems
diffuse cerebral issues with multifocal deficits
general brain impairment with various neurological signs

pathognomonic.symptomName: Progressive cognitive decline including memory impairment and executive dysfunction
searchTerms: gradual memory loss and thinking problems
progressive cognitive decline with executive dysfunction

common.symptomName: Seizures of focal or generalized type
searchTerms: seizures affecting part or whole brain

common.symptomName: Headache due to increased intracranial pressure
searchTerms: head pain from increased intracranial pressure
weakness on one side of body

occasional.symptomName: Nausea and vomiting related to raised intracranial pressure
searchTerms: nausea and vomiting from brain pressure
vomiting related to increased head pressure
feeling sick due to raised intracranial pressure

rare.symptomName: Endocrine dysfunction due to hypothalamic involvement
searchTerms: hormone problems from brain area damage
endocrine issues due to hypothalamus involvement
hormonal imbalance caused by brain tumor

rare.symptomName: Hydrocephalus secondary to CSF flow obstruction
searchTerms: fluid buildup in brain from blockage
brain swelling due to blocked fluid flow
cranial nerve palsies causing facial or eye problems

laboratory: CSF analysis typically non-specific; may show mild protein elevation
imaging: MRI demonstrating diffuse T2/FLAIR hyperintensity involving at least three cerebral lobes
Lack of a discrete enhancing mass lesion
Possible mild mass effect without significant edema
genetic: Frequent IDH1/IDH2 mutations in some cases
TP53 mutations and ATRX loss reported
other: Histopathology showing diffuse infiltration of glial tumor cells with variable cellularity and mitotic activity

distinguishingFeatures: More localized tumor mass on imaging
Less extensive involvement of multiple lobes
Histopathology showing more circumscribed tumor margins
Presence of inflammatory markers in CSF
Fever and systemic signs of infection
MRI showing patchy enhancement and edema
Non-neoplastic white matter changes on MRI
Absence of tumor cells on biopsy
Clinical history of toxic, metabolic, or demyelinating cause

redFlags: Diffuse involvement of three or more cerebral lobes on MRI
Failure to respond to standard treatments for inflammatory or infectious encephalopathies
references: Louis DN, et al. WHO Classification of Tumours of the Central Nervous System, 5th Edition. IARC, 2021.
Kepes JJ. Gliomatosis cerebri: a clinical and pathological study of 26 cases. Cancer. 1979.
Wen PY, Kesari S. Malignant gliomas in adults. N Engl J Med. 2008.
